sourcedFrom:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The 605 is a five-shot .357 Magnum on Taurus's small frame, and it is covered inside the big REVOLVERS book - one manual carrying roughly 67 models at once. That is the thing to hold on to throughout: a procedure printed under another model's heading in this book does not apply to your 605 just because it is on the same page. The 605 is a fixed-sight gun with a 2-inch barrel, and Taurus publishes no disassembly for it at all.

steps.title: Find your 605 in the book's own table before anything else
steps.action: The 605 sits in the SMALL FRAME FIXED SIGHTS REVOLVERS table: .357 Magnum, DA/SA, five rounds, 2-inch barrel, fixed sights. Note the word FIXED - it is the heading of the whole table, and it decides which of this book's sight sections apply to you.
steps.prose: One book, sixty-odd revolvers, six specification tables. Reading the wrong row is not a small error here: the 410 PD two columns away is a .45 Colt/.410 gun, and the 905 sharing the 605's own column pair is a 9mm that takes stellar clips. The caliber stamped on your barrel is the authority, and the table is how you find the right row under it.
steps.aside: One substitution is allowed and it is worth knowing: Taurus states .38 Special ammunition may be used in all their revolvers chambered for .357 Magnum. They also say these are the only caliber substitutions that will function.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Small Frame Fixed Sights Revolvers - specifications, printed p.12 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Thumb piece forward - and your 605 is NOT on the front-latch list
steps.action: Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and press the cylinder out to the left at the same time. Do not go looking for a front latch: the book lists exactly which models need one pressed simultaneously - Models 30, 218, 416, 454, 444, 45, 513 and 513UL - and the 605 is not among them.
steps.prose: This is the clearest case in the whole book of a procedure that is model-scoped rather than general, and Taurus flags it with an ATTENTION line for that reason. On a 605 one latch is all there is; if the cylinder resists, the hammer is not fully down or a case head is under the star, and pressing harder on an imaginary second latch will only bend something.
steps.quote: LOADING THE CYLINDER FOR .357 MAGNUM / .38 SPECIAL With the thumb of the right hand, push the thumb piece forward and at the same time press the cylinder, swinging it out to the left. ATTENTION: On Model 30, Model 218, Model 416, Model 454, Model 444, Model 45, Model 513 and Model 513UL using the left thumb, press down the front latch simultaneously.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Muzzle up, one firm push, five chambers
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. All five cases lift together on the star; confirm every one has left the cylinder.
steps.prose: A .357 Magnum case is long, and a 2-inch 605's ejector rod is correspondingly short - it does not give you the full case length of travel, so a half-hearted push genuinely can leave a case standing proud that then drops back as the star returns. Muzzle up and one decisive stroke; if a case still sticks, a rod from the muzzle is the answer, not more force on the extractor.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Stellar clips are a feature of certain models - your 605 is not one
steps.action: If you have read about Taurus stellar clips, note that the book scopes them to certain models: they hold rimless cartridges in the cylinder, and rimless means 9mm or .45 ACP. A .357 Magnum 605 headspaces on the case rim and takes no clip.
steps.prose: The reason this belongs in a 605 guide is that the 905 shares the 605's column in the specification table and IS the 9mm gun that uses them - so the clip material sits a few lines away from your model's row. Trying to seat a clip in a 605 cylinder, or leaving one on the bench and assuming it belongs to this gun, is exactly the mistake proximity in a category book produces.
steps.quote: TAURUS STELLAR CLIP Certain models of Taurus revolvers utilize the Taurus Stellar Clip to hold "rimless" cartridges in place in the cylinder.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Taurus Stellar Clip, printed p.33 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: The two sight sections are both scoped - and neither is your 605's
steps.action: This book prints an 'External Adjustable Sight Models Only' procedure with elevation and windage screws. Your 605 is in the FIXED SIGHTS table, so that section does not describe it - there is nothing on a 605 to turn, and no adjustment to lose during a clean.
steps.prose: Read the heading before the procedure, every time. A fixed-sight snub's zero is set by the barrel and the front sight blade, so if a 605 shoots off point of impact the answer is ammunition or technique, not a screwdriver. The practical upside is that you can wipe the topstrap freely without worrying about moving anything.
steps.quote: External Adjustable Sight Models Only To adjust, make sure the firearm is unloaded and always keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. If possible, leave the cylinder open during adjustment.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.36 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: And the integral-adjustable section is scoped too
steps.action: The second sight section covers an integral adjustable sight whose blade moves left and right only, from a screw on the top right of the frame. That is also a 'Models Only' section and also not the 605, which has a fixed rear notch cut into the topstrap.
steps.prose: Two adjacent 'Models Only' headings, two different mechanisms, and neither belongs to your revolver - that is what a 67-model book looks like from the inside. If you find no adjustment screw anywhere on your frame, that is not a missing part; it is confirmation you are reading the right table row.
steps.quote: Integral Adjustable Sight Models Only The sight blade may be adjusted from left to right only (windage).
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.36 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: Cylinder out, five chambers looked into and felt
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber. That is the working state for the entire clean.
steps.prose: Both senses, and the reason is the same on a 605 as on any dark-chambered .357: a brass case head deep in a chamber reads as chamber wall to the eye at bench-light angles. Five chambers is a small enough count that there is no excuse for losing your place, so go round once in one direction and stop where you started.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Lead, not just carbon - a .357 snub strips it into the forcing cone
steps.action: After shooting, get all powder residue out of the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush. If you find lead particles in the barrel, scrub them out with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate as described. Clean before more than 200 rounds go through in a row.
steps.prose: This matters on a 605 in particular because .38 Special practice loads are usually cast lead and a 2-inch .357 barrel is almost all forcing cone and first inches of rifling - exactly where lead strips off and stays. Leading raises pressure, and a gun chambered for .357 Magnum is not the place to let pressure creep. Wet brass brush, never steel and never dry.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, it is of special importance that all residues of powder be removed from barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, using an appropriate brush. If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Nothing here transfers to a look-alike
steps.action: Take this as belonging to the 605 designation and the models named alongside it in the book's own exploded-view list, and nowhere else. Taurus prints the warning: look-alike firearms differ widely in the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: The 605 shares an exploded view with sixteen other Taurus designations, and it shares a silhouette with a great many small revolvers from other makers whose cylinder latches move the other way. If pushing the latch toward the muzzle does nothing, stop - you are not holding a Taurus 605.
steps.aside: The book's own exploded view for this family is headed: Models: 17C, 17 C UL, 410 PD, 605, 905, 73, 731, 731 UL, 85 RB, 85 85ti, 85 UL, 85 UL/Ti, 650, 850, 850 UL/Ti, 651, 851.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Field strip complete - and the barrel stays on
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, five chambers empty. That is the whole 605 field strip. Taurus states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly needed and then says plainly: do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.prose: Where disassembly genuinely is necessary the book's route is the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer - not the bench. The exploded view at the back is a parts list headed with a model line; it has no sequence attached and is not an instruction to take anything off.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus REVOLVERS book publishes no disassembly for any of the roughly 67 models it covers. Its care section opens by saying the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly and then adds, flatly, 'Do not disassemble the barrel.' Where disassembly is genuinely necessary it routes the revolver to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The nine exploded views at the back are parts diagrams headed with model lists; none of them carries an order of operations. There is nothing published past the cylinder-open clean, so nothing deeper is walked - and borrowing a sideplate procedure from another maker's book would be exactly the substitution this rebuild exists to stop.

cleaning.name: BORE, FORCING CONE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Remove all powder residue from the barrel and the adjacent areas with an appropriate brush
If lead particles are detected in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate
Work the forcing cone hardest - on a 2-inch .357 it takes almost all of the gas cutting and leading
Brush all five chambers and follow with a dry patch; a .357 chamber fired with .38 Special builds a step at the shorter case mouth that makes magnum cases stick
Check the bore for light before the revolver goes away

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACE, STAR & CRANE
tasks: Take the carbon ring off the front face of the cylinder - it is what eventually stops the cylinder closing
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under the star holds it proud and the cylinder will not close on it
Wipe the crane and the frame window and check the cylinder sits flush when closed
Do not use any abrasive material anywhere on the cylinder - the book bans it outright on titanium models and it is bad practice on all of them

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, OIL & STORAGE
tasks: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and proceed the same way through the bore; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush
Do not keep the revolver in contact with materials that attract moisture or acidic materials, and avoid cloth holsters that retain moisture
For long storage take extra care with the metal surfaces against corrosion
A revolver with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Nothing was removed, so nothing is refitted. Let the extractor rod return fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently until it latches - never flick it shut, which knocks a small-frame crane out of true and starts the cylinder binding.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and feel the stop drop into each of the five notches.
fncheck: With all five chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch under light thumb pressure with no perceptible side play; hand rotation should feel the cylinder stop engage at each notch; the hammer should hold at full cock without following; the transfer bar must stay clear of the firing pin until the trigger is pulled fully through and drop back as it returns; and both single and double action should reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Taurus's standing advice for their revolvers is to carry with an empty chamber under the hammer and never with the hammer cocked or the trigger held to the rear.
